title: Speech & Language Therapy
shortDescription: Expert speech and language therapy to help individuals communicate effectively and overcome speech delays, articulation issues, and language disorders.
features: Individualized speech assessments and customized intervention plans
Articulation and pronunciation training for clear verbal communication
Expressive and receptive language skill development
Alternative and Augmentative Communication (AAC) support
Fluency / Stuttering therapy and voice modulation

faqs.question: What is Speech and Language Therapy?
faqs.answer: Speech and Language Therapy provides treatment, support and care for children and adults who have difficulties with communication, eating, drinking or swallowing.

faqs.question: When should a child start speech therapy?
faqs.answer: Early intervention is key. If a child is not meeting speech milestones (such as not babbling by 12 months, or lack of words by 18-24 months), an evaluation should be scheduled immediately.

faqs.question: How long does speech therapy take?
faqs.answer: The duration varies based on the individual needs and severity of the condition. Many children show remarkable progress within a few months of regular sessions.

title: Occupational Therapy (OT)
shortDescription: Helping children develop fine motor skills, sensory processing abilities, hand-eye coordination, and daily life independence.
features: Fine and gross motor skills enhancement through therapeutic play
Sensory Integration Therapy for sensory processing challenges
Self-care training (dressing, feeding, grooming, writing)
Visual-spatial awareness and bilateral coordination exercises
Adaptive equipment recommendations and environmental modifications

faqs.question: How does Occupational Therapy help my child?
faqs.answer: Occupational Therapy helps children participate in the things they want and need to do through the therapeutic use of everyday activities (occupations).

faqs.question: What is Sensory Integration?
faqs.answer: Sensory integration is how our brain organizes and processes information from our senses (touch, movement, body awareness, sight, sound). OT helps children process sensory inputs effectively.

title: ABA (Applied Behavior Analysis) Therapy
shortDescription: Evidence-based behavioral intervention to improve positive social behaviors, focus, communication, and reduce challenging behaviors.
features: Positive reinforcement techniques for learning new skills
Functional Behavior Assessments (FBA) to understand triggers
Social skills training and peer interaction programs
Parent and caregiver training for consistent home support
Targeted reduction of maladaptive behaviors

faqs.question: What is ABA Therapy?
faqs.answer: Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) is a scientifically validated approach to understanding behavior and how it is affected by the environment.

faqs.question: Who benefits most from ABA therapy?
faqs.answer: ABA therapy is particularly effective for individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), ADHD, and other developmental and behavioral challenges.

title: Art Therapy & Creative Expression
shortDescription: Therapeutic creative arts to foster emotional healing, self-expression, cognitive development, and stress relief in a nurturing space.
features: Non-verbal emotional expression through painting, sculpting, and drawing
Boosts self-esteem, focus, and emotional regulation
Promotes fine motor dexterity and visual-spatial imagination
Therapeutic safe space guided by compassionate therapists

faqs.question: Does my child need to be good at art for Art Therapy?
faqs.answer: Not at all! Art therapy is about the creative process and emotional expression, not artistic skill or creating a masterpiece.

title: Early Learning & Development
shortDescription: Play-based early childhood education designed to build cognitive, social, and emotional foundations for lifelong learning.
features: Play-based curriculum stimulating curiosity and discovery
Language, literacy, and numeracy foundations
Social-emotional skill building in small group settings
Holistic physical and cognitive development

faqs.question: What age group is Early Learning suitable for?
faqs.answer: Our early learning programs are tailored for toddlers and young children aged 2 to 5 years.

title: Inclusive Preschool Program
shortDescription: Nurturing preschool environment integrating specialized care with standard developmental milestones.
features: Structured daily routine with fun interactive activities
Inclusive classroom environment fostering empathy and friendship
School-readiness preparation for smooth school transitions

faqs.question: How does Cares Preschool differ from regular preschools?
faqs.answer: We provide specialized attention, lower student-to-teacher ratios, and integrated therapy support in an inclusive, warm atmosphere.

title: Special Education Program
shortDescription: Tailored educational curricula designed for neurodiverse learners, ensuring every child learns at their own pace.
features: Individualized Education Plans (IEP) customized for each learner
Multi-sensory teaching methodologies
Functional academic and practical life skills training
Close collaboration between special educators, therapists, and parents

faqs.question: What is an IEP?
faqs.answer: An Individualized Education Plan (IEP) is a personalized educational roadmap crafted for a specific child to target their unique learning goals and milestones.

title: Educational Consultancy & Guidance
shortDescription: Comprehensive assessment, school placement advice, and parental guidance for children with special educational needs.
features: Detailed developmental and educational assessments
School readiness and mainstream inclusion consultation
Parental counseling and home-support strategies

faqs.question: Who should seek educational consultancy?
faqs.answer: Parents looking for guidance on school readiness, specialized intervention, or selecting the right academic environment for their child.
